infra_bot: INCIDENT AUTO-PAGER: Elevated 5xx + upstream timeouts in region us-central1. Thresholds breached (5m avg). Pager: @sre_oncall
sre_oncall: acknowledging, looking
sre_oncall: can folks post links to dashboards? datadog: https://d.datadog/xyz/redwood/us-central1
eng_prod: saw spike ~11:37 UTC, 5xx rate ~18% on gateway edges to ml-workers, latency tail >4s
ops_lead: customer reports: webhooks failing, some retries causing duplicate charges. cs linked ticket RW-4532
maya_r: are we seeing Redis/KV evictions? I see a TTL surge on prefix-cache keys
ml_runtime: logs show a KV cache miss storm, many requests fell back to cold model initialization -> downstream worker saturate
alex_k: what triggered the cache misses? deploys? config change?
eng_prod: no deploys in last 2 hours. There was a rate-limit change to routing policy earlier but we rolled that back at 11:20
sre_oncall: running quick query: `SELECT count(*) FROM proxy_errors WHERE region='us-central1' AND code LIKE '5%'` -> high
ops_lead: starting cross-region shift: propose steer ~20% traffic to us-east2 for 5m while we triage
sre_oncall: +1, start steering via smart-routing immediately. Eng, prepare rollback if errors appear in us-east2
eng_prod: creating temporary route: `reroute --from us-central1 --to us-east2 --pct 20 --reason 'mitigate cache storm'`
infra_bot: ROUTE CHANGE: initiated by eng_prod at 11:45 UTC. Policy id: rt-7782
maya_r: confirming KV memory: redis-primary-us-central1 at 92% used and spike in evictions. TTLs falling from 24h->5m for several prefixes
ml_runtime: I suspect a prefix-eviction pattern: some consumer started writing with a wildcard TTL override. Searching for recent jobs...
alex_k: grep in deploy logs shows a cron job from analytics wrote keys with `setex prefix:* 300` at 11:32 — that's suspicious
ops_lead: can we block that job? maya, can you kill the job and restore TTLs from snapshot?
maya_r: killed analytics job PID 2345. Restoring TTL defaults via script. `redis-cli` commands queued.
eng_prod: still seeing 5xx but reduced to ~9% after the 20% reroute and job kill
sre_oncall: spinning up emergency cache-resilience: enable prefix-level read-through policy and enforce reserved cache slots for model workers
eng_prod: applied cache reservation config `cache.reserved = model_workers:1024` — infra accepted
infra_bot: SCALE ACTION: added 4x ml-worker instances in us-central1 (hot standby) at 11:55 UTC
ml_runtime: p95 latency dropping to 1.2s, 5xx at 4.5% now
customer_success: notifying affected customers with status note: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1777777777
ops_lead: are we comfortable to ramp traffic back? propose 50% -> 100% over 15m
sre_oncall: let's monitor 10m windows, if errors <2% and no downstream queueing, proceed
eng_prod: ramping to 50% at 12:05 UTC
infra_bot: ROUTE CHANGE: ramp to 50% completed
ml_runtime: metrics look stable, queue lengths normalizing
alex_k: we should add a runbook step: detect sudden TTL drops and auto-block jobs that set short TTLs for critical prefixes
sre_oncall: agreed, filing follow-up action: RW-4533 (runbook + guardrails). Assign eng_prod + maya_r
customer_success: sent interim customer update, offered postmortem once root cause confirmed
ops_lead: marking incident as mitigated for paging. On-call handoff to day SRE for monitoring and follow-up
sre_oncall: handing off to lina_day (oncall) for 12:30-20:30 shift. Final checks in 30m
lina_day: acknowledged, will watch for 2 hours and escalate if regression
sre_oncall: closing pager, leaving channel for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
infra_bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: state=mitigated, severity=sev2, start=1777777777, mitigated=1777778060
